extracted.intended_audience: authors of interactive fiction (ChoiceScript writers) submitting to the Choice of Games contest
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a full-length ChoiceScript interactive novel to the Choice of Games Contest, meeting technical, eligibility, and judging standards for publication and prizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written in ChoiceScript and English
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter the contest, your game must: Be written in ChoiceScript, in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be implemented using ChoiceScript. The game text and interface must be in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length: minimum words and playthrough length
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter the contest, your game must be at least 100,000 words long, including both prose and code, with a playthrough length of at least 20,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word counts include prose and ChoiceScript code. The 'playthrough' length is the amount a player reads in a single playthrough; this must be at least 20,000 words. Judges will also evaluate whether the game is the right length for its story (neither too rushed nor too slow) under the 'Length and Coding Efficiency' judging criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated tests: Quicktest and Randomtest
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter the contest, your game must pass both Quicktest and Randomtest automated tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must run and pass ChoiceScript's Quicktest and Randomtest to ensure stability and basic functioning before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Player character gender choice
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter the contest, the game must allow players to choose the player character’s gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contest entries are required to include gender choice for the player character; Hosted Games submissions do not have this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author eligibility: age and residency
rubrics_metrics.description: The author(s) must be over the age of 18 as of January 31, 2018 and reside in the fifty United States or Washington, D.C., the United Kingdom, or Canada (except Quebec).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team submissions are allowed but team members must all meet the residency and age requirements. If you think you may be ineligible, email contest-ineligible@choiceofgames.com to explain; feedback may influence future contests. Hosted Games allows authors of any age and from most countries (with some tax-treaty considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Team size limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple authors can submit a game as a team, but the team can have no more than 5 members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All team members must meet the residency and age requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges may disqualify for failing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The judges may disqualify a game if it entirely fails to meet one or more of these standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: an incomprehensible game might be disqualified for prose styling. This is a strict enforcement note: failing key standards (e.g., prose incomprehension, not meeting technical requirements) can lead to disqualification rather than low scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original, Interesting Characters (15%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment questions: Does each character have a distinct personality and voice? Does the dialogue feel natural? Do the characters’ personalities and plots avoid overused tropes?

rubrics_metrics.name: Original, Interesting Setting and Plot (15%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Original, Interesting Setting and Plot: 15% of score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment questions: Is the setting unusual? Is the setting well-communicated through descriptions and characters? Does the plot branch in meaningful and interesting ways? Does the plot proceed in a natural and cohesive manner?

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting Goals with Satisfying Endings (15%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicting Goals with Satisfying Endings: 15% of score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment questions: Are there multiple things for the player’s character to want? Are there multiple satisfying ways for the player’s character to achieve their goals? Are there multiple potential happy endings? Are there interesting and difficult tradeoffs between different goals? Does the game effectively communicate to the player why they reached the ending that they did?

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced, Intentional, Interesting Choices/Options (15%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Balanced, Intentional, Interesting Choices/Options: 15% of score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment questions: Do the player’s choices lead to meaningful differences in the story? Does the game effectively communicate the potential effects of the player’s choices? Do the options give roughly equal chances of success? Does the game avoid surprise advantages or disadvantages? Are there interesting and difficult tradeoffs to be made in the player’s choices?

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity (10%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment questions: Do the characters reflect the full diversity of the society in which the game is set? Are all types of people (especially groups traditionally underrepresented in media) treated respectfully and non-stereotypically? If there is romance in the game, are there equally satisfying romance options regardless of the player character’s orientation?

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose Styling (10%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment questions: Are the sentences in the game beautiful? Are they well-constructed? Are individual words well-chosen? Does the tone fit the theme? Is the spelling and grammar correct? Note: gross failures in prose (e.g., incomprehensible text) may lead to disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Stats, Consistently Applied (10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative Stats, Consistently Applied: 10% of score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment questions: Are the skills balanced, with no single skill being much more useful than the others? Do the stats communicate something about the game’s theme? Do the stats track story effects in useful and interesting ways? Are there meaningful secondary stats which track against the player’s goals?

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and Coding Efficiency (5%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length and Coding Efficiency: 5% of score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment questions: How many words do players read each time they play (playthrough length)? Is each playthrough long enough? Is the game the right length for the story that it’s trying to tell: neither too rushed nor too slow? Is the code executed efficiently, with a minimum of cut-and-paste scenes?

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall / Judge’s Choice (5%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment questions: Does your game feel like a 'Choice of Games' game? (See public guidelines for authors to understand what they're looking for and how to outline your game.) Do we just love your game? This is a subjective catch-all for judges' overall impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta testing recommended (not required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beta testing is strongly encouraged but not formally required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are strongly encouraged to beta test their game, either privately with selected testers or in a public beta. The forum is suggested as a place to recruit beta testers. While not mandatory, the page notes it's 'almost impossible to write great material without anyone else’s feedback.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosted Games publishing standards (comparison/guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosted Games (HG) has different/looser standards and different length/minimums than the contest and forbids deeply offensive material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosted Games minimum length for publication is 30,000 words (contest requires 100,000). HG does not require allowing player gender choice. HG forbids deeply offensive material (e.g., scenes that glorify sexual violence or racist attitudes) though it allows some material that the main Choice of Games label may handle differently. If you don't qualify for the contest, consider submitting to Hosted Games.
